newsitem.title: USA: Senate finally confirms Raines as budget chief.
newsitem.headline: Senate finally confirms Raines as budget chief.

text.p: The Senate confirmed Franklin Raines as White House budget director Friday, months after President Clinton announced his choice last spring.

Raines, 47, was confirmed on a voice vote. He is vice chairman and director of the Federal National Mortgage Association, which arranges mortgage packages for investors, and a spokesman there said Raines will assume his new post as director of the Office of the Management and Budget next week.
The primary role of the director of OMB is to prepare the presidential budget.
The Senate acted on a voice vote with only a few senators on the floor. There were no objections.

"This is the right thing to do," said Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, a Mississippi Republican, as he offered the nomination. "I'm satisfied he is eminently qualified for the position, and the president should have his director of the Office of Management and Budget in place."

Raines was picked to replace Alice Rivlin, who was chosen to be vice chairman of the Federal Reserve. But Rivlin's nomination was held up for months over a disagreement about approving Alan Greenspan for a new term as Fed chairman.

Testifying in July before the Senate Committee on Governmental Affairs, which approved his nomination, Raines said the job of the budget director was "to actually deliver on the promise the administration and Congress have made to the American people to balance the federal budget by 2002 and reduce the burden of the national debt."
